facts.content: Patient has had 3 days of diarrhea with vomiting and fever.
facts.source_text: CC: 3 days of diarrhea with vomiting and fever

facts.content: Diarrhea started as watery and now is very loose with more than 4 stools today.
facts.source_text: Diarrhea started watery, now very loose; ~≥4 stools today; lost count

facts.content: Patient feels feverish, described as 'boiling,' and is vomiting everything including water and tea.
facts.source_text: Assoc sx: feverish “boiling,” vomiting everything incl water/tea

facts.content: Patient experiences intermittent periumbilical crampy pain and urge to defecate.
facts.source_text: periumbilical crampy pain, intermittent, urge to defecate

facts.content: There is no blood in stool or urine.
facts.source_text: no blood in stool/urine

facts.content: The last vomiting episode was about 2 hours before the call after breakfast.
facts.source_text: Last emesis: ~2 hrs prior to call after breakfast

facts.content: The patient voided urine about 1 hour ago, but color was not assessed.
facts.source_text: Urine: voided ~1 hr ago; color not assessed; passing urine

facts.content: Patient's brother has similar symptoms and there is a reported school outbreak.
facts.source_text: Sick contact: brother with similar sx; reports school outbreak

facts.content: There has been no travel and the patient's diet was normal prior to symptoms.
facts.source_text: Triggers: no travel; diet normal prior

facts.content: Patient attempted self-care with Oral Rehydration Solution three times a day for two days but is not improving due to vomiting.
facts.source_text: Self-care: ORS (salt-sugar) ~3x/day x2 days; not improving due to emesis

facts.content: Patient has no prior abdominal issues except for menstrual cramps.
facts.source_text: PMH/PSH: no prior abd issues; menstrual cramps only

facts.content: Patient takes vitamin D daily and ibuprofen as needed for dysmenorrhea.
facts.source_text: Meds: vitamin D daily; ibuprofen PRN dysmenorrhea

facts.content: Patient is a graphic designer working from home due to illness and lives with brother and mother.
facts.source_text: SH: Graphic designer; WFH due to illness; lives with brother and mother

facts.content: Patient does not smoke and drinks alcohol occasionally.
facts.source_text: Habits: No smoking; occasional alcohol (pint from time to time)

facts.content: Patient has no rash.
facts.source_text: ROS: No rash

facts.content: Acute gastroenteritis is likely infectious, either viral or foodborne, with 3 days of diarrhea, vomiting, fever, and crampy abdominal pain.
facts.source_text: Acute gastroenteritis (likely infectious, viral vs foodborne; household contact positive). Features: 3 days watery→loose diarrhea, vomiting, feverish, crampy periumbilical pain, no blood.

facts.content: There is a risk of dehydration due to ongoing vomiting, but the patient is still producing urine.
facts.source_text: Risk of dehydration due to ongoing emesis; still producing urine 1 hr prior.

facts.content: Continue using Oral Rehydration Solution in tiny frequent sips and maintain oral intake as tolerated.
facts.source_text: Hydration: Continue ORS in tiny frequent sips; maintain oral intake as tolerated

facts.content: Follow a simple diet like BRAT, avoid dairy and fruits/vegetables initially, and advance as tolerated.
facts.source_text: Diet: Simple/BRAT-like foods (toast/biscuits); avoid dairy, fruit/veg initially; advance as tolerated

facts.content: Arrange urgent stool sample for culture/PCR according to clinic protocol.
facts.source_text: Diagnostics: Arrange urgent stool sample for culture/PCR per clinic protocol

facts.content: Urgent in-person clinic appointment is needed to assess hydration status and submit stool sample.
facts.source_text: Assessment: Urgent in-person clinic appt to assess hydration status and submit stool sample

facts.content: Visit A&E/urgent care if unable to keep fluids down, reduced urine output, persistent high fever, worsening abdominal pain, blood in stool, confusion/lethargy, or symptoms last more than 7 days.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: A&E/urgent care if unable to keep fluids down, reduced urine output, persistent high fever, worsening abd pain, blood in stool, confusion/lethargy, or symptoms >7 days

facts.content: Continue working from home and rest as needed.
facts.source_text: Work: Continue WFH/rest as needed

facts.content: Follow-up should be booked via support line and patient should call back if there is deterioration before the appointment.
facts.source_text: Follow-up: Book via support line; call back if deterioration before appointment
